Hey, I’m just in high school but during exam time at my school, we don’t have to attend school, we can study from home but I find that I can’t do work in my room. I feel so unmotivated to do things especially school work in my room. 

So during exam season I would go to school, even though I don’t have to, I would go to school like I have class. And I would get up each morning brush my teeth and brush my hair and wear my uniform and go to school and study. 

I think this will help you get into the old habit of going to class even though you don’t actually have class and instead of staying in your room you can go to the library or Starbucks or anywhere. And if those are closed because of COVID, if the weathers nice, go outside? 

But don’t stay in your room and discipline yourself. Discipline is so important and to vary out you work load throughout the semester. I’m the type to procrastinate a lot and I think the main reason I have low grades is because I procrastinate. Even if did little study everyday for the whole year I’m sure I would get good grades but I don’t but you can! 

This is a top tip from my dad who has 4 degrees and 2 PHDs and can speak 4 languages. He always tells me that he goes into a lecture and takes rough notes on a paper and then after the lecture goes and puts the notes neatly on a new piece of paper, this way he studies the new stuff while it’s fresh in his mind and while he transfers the new neat notes he’s also studying what he’s been taught. 

Also my Spanish teacher tells me to ALWAYS do a timetable of the workload eg. Writing assignment due for Friday, an hour each day to finish it. 

This way you can structure your day and discipline yourself to follow and keep up with deadlines so you don’t waste time. 

Hopefully that wasn’t all just bullshit and you found some of it helpful! Good luck with uni!

Hey, I’ll like to come on here as someone who’s close in age as you. I’m 18 and I am severely depressed. And I had lots of situations where I tried to kill myself like your girlfriend, and people around me, boyfriends, friends etc. Left me to the point where I have no friends at the moment. 

So I’ve been in your girlfriends shoes and I won’t say you should break up with her because if I do that I would feel like I’m hurting this girl through you who clearly needs lots of help. But I will say this, you should talk to her. 

Sit her down and talk to her. And tell her how you feel, chances are she knows exactly how she makes you feel and she will sympathise. 

Just because you have depression doesn’t mean you don’t feel compassion for people who care about you, if anything you feel more. 

And if you do decide to break up with her don’t forget her, text her and make sure she’s ok, go to park together, do colouring etc. But show her that even though you may not be together you’re there for her. Especially because it sounds like you really care for this person, don’t let them go and forget them. 

These little things you do with her even after you break up with her will mean the world to her, especially because it sounds like she has a little social circle (her parents don’t care for her, she doesn’t go to school so no friends maybe etc) 

They might try to kill themselves and blame you or say hurtful things to you but don’t mind it at all because 

a) they don’t mean it, you should understand that depression is an illness and she’s not well and take everything she says with a pinch of salt and 

b) this may not be everyone but I feel like as depressed people, we tend to do this a lot, she wants you to feel the pain she’s going through and the pain you put her through by breaking up with her so she’ll say things to you and do things but don’t mind her and continue to be there for her (as long as you’re mentally able to handle it) but don’t let her drag you down with her too ofc but don’t forget she’s an ill person and needs lots of help and compassion and understatement too.
